purpose: Build the regional landscape from available evidence while further map transcription proceeds separately.

marshPrior.authority: User working expectation for marsh without better observations, 2 October 2026
marshPrior.policy: Use about 12 ft as the unsurveyed marsh prior within identified historical marsh footprints. Historical ground and ordinary street observations take precedence; banks, structures and works margins do not establish marsh height. Apply no such default to the whole valley or terrace. Blend only the outer modelling transition into adjoining relief; retain explicit estimated status.

localMarshEstimates.method: Use the existing reviewed field compartment, excluding a 5 m edge strip reserved for banks and transitions. Interpolate 11.2/10.8 ft ground levels along northing, clamping beyond the two observed northings. These constrain a gently graded marsh estimate, not modern fill or a cottage-garden level.
localMarshEstimates.reason: The user identifies these marsh-edge observations as lower than the 13.9 ft Knobshill Cottage garden. Their 0.4 ft difference supports only about 12 cm northward rise; modern terrain does not justify larger interior relief.

streetPolicy: Use historical street and marsh-lane levels without a blanket fill subtraction. Adjacent ground may differ; preserve reviewed local relief.
earlierMarshPolicy: Under the user's working assumption, a reviewed 1848-51 marsh-ground observation is a lower-bound estimate for 1900 where the same land surface survives. Later fill or building development may raise it. Retain original date, datum and surface role; do not treat banks, decks, benchmarks or channel beds as marsh ground. Specific evidence of excavation or a changed channel requires local review.
earlierMarshStatus: Selected 1848–51 regional review now supplies 45 early low-lane and ground-margin proxies. They establish representative marsh levels under the author’s continuity assumption; they are not 45 interior marsh surveys.
modernReliefPolicy: Modern relief is a fallback outside the broad historical marsh envelope only. Within that envelope the early regional marsh surface takes precedence, with later ground and bounded raised-surface evidence.
boundaryPolicy: Corrections propagate only along dry grid edges that do not intersect mapped water or reviewed canal/structure exclusions. Exclusions are not hydraulic barrier heights.
missingDataPolicy: Retain missing cells where neither modern terrain nor accepted historical interpolation supplies a height. No zero-height fallback.
surfaceHierarchy: Regional 1848–51 marsh estimate; later ground corrections; later streets and factory yards confined to mapped footprints; bank/wall margins and railway/sewer formations confined to their own footprints. Benchmarks do not become ground or crest heights.
